summary: This note is a short encyclopedia-style entry on Irondequoit Bay, a large body of water in northeastern Monroe County, New York. It describes the bay's inflow from Irondequoit Creek, its outflow into Lake Ontario, and the location of its deepest point near the Irondequoit Bay Bridge that carries New York State Route 104. The note's width, length, elevation and depth figures are missing from the source text.
one_line: Irondequoit Bay is a large body of water in northeastern Monroe County, New York, fed by Irondequoit Creek and draining into Lake Ontario.
key_facts: Irondequoit Bay is a large body of water located in northeastern Monroe County, New York.
Irondequoit Bay is fed by Irondequoit Creek to the south.
Irondequoit Bay flows into Lake Ontario at its northern end.
The Irondequoit Bay Bridge carries the six-lane New York State Route 104 over Irondequoit Bay.
The deepest point of Irondequoit Bay is a short distance north of the Irondequoit Bay Bridge.
The note describes Irondequoit Bay as roughly wide and in length, but the width and length figures are missing from the source text.
The note states the average surface elevation of Irondequoit Bay above sea level, but the numeric value is missing from the source text.
The note states the depth of Irondequoit Bay at its deepest point, but the numeric value is missing from the source text.
